chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem narrated to us, and he narrated to me from Ar-Rayyan ibn As-Salt,

He said: When I intended to depart for Iraq, I resolved to bid farewell to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him). I said to myself: When I bid him farewell, I will ask him for a shirt from the garments of his body to be used as my shroud, and dirhams from his wealth with which I will make rings for my daughters. When I bid him farewell, weeping and sorrow over parting from him occupied me, so I forgot to ask him for that. When I exited from before him, he called out to me, 'O Rayyan, return!' So I returned, and he said to me: 'Do you not love that I give you a shirt from the garments of my body, in which you will be shrouded when your term ends? Or do you not love that I give you dirhams with which you will make rings for your daughters?' I said: 'O my master, it was in my mind to ask you for that, but grief over parting from you prevented me.' So he (peace be upon him) lifted the cushion, brought out a shirt and gave it to me, and lifted the side of the prayer rug, brought out dirhams and gave them to me. I counted them, and they were thirty dirhams.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (a title of Imam Ali al-Ridha, peace be upon him)
key_terms.لِكَفِّنَ بِهِ: To be used as a shroud for burial

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.) give to Ar-Rayyan ibn As-Salt when he bid him farewell?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s *‘ilm al-ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) regarding Rayyan’s inner intentions, a key indicator of divine leadership (*Imamah*) in Shia theology. The specific gift of thirty dirhams and the shirt for shrouding underscores the concept of *karamat* (miracles of the Imams) and the spiritual benefit of possessing physical relics (*athar*) of the Ahl al-Bayt for the faithful.
